newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MAY 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MAY 20.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis yesterday forecast that inflation would fall further than 5.5 percent in May, during last night's Parliament debate on the economy with conservative opposition New Democracy leader Costas Karamanlis.
--The finance ministry yesterday considered the extent of state participation in the forthcoming National Bank share capital increase.
--Red tape and dissenting views have held up funding and modernisation work totalling 35.7 billion drachmas for the Greek Post Offices.

--Transport and Communications Minister Haris Kastanidis said yesterday that he would brief the leaders of all political parties on Olympic Airway's one trillion drachma procurements programme for new aircraft.

--The general price index yesterday inched closer to an all-time record, closing at 1,670.23 points, up 1.92 percent. The picture on the Athens bourse is particularly encouraging, brokers say, with strong interest from large and small private investors.

--A committee of experts has recommended new measures to bring inflation to 5.5 percent by the end of the year, rather than the 4.5 forecast. The committee's report will be handed to Prime Minister Costas Simitis and National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou within the week.

--Greece is within reach of inclusion in economic and monetary union in 1999 if the government's economic policies continue slowly and surely in the next two years, Simitis affirmed yesterday during his debate. He warned however that the time left to Greece was not great.
--The Greek National Tourism Organisation is to close down tourist offices that are not officially approved by the organisation.

--There was no decision after yesterday's meeting on how to reschedule debts owed banks from the Organisations of Ailing Enterprises. The debts come to come 90 billion drachmas and the state is considering covering this debt with state bonds.
--ND leader Costas Karamanlis said the pace of greece's course to convergence was slow and that real convergence was not a prospect.
--The European Investment Bank has given the go-ahead for a loan of 220 billion drachmas for the construction of the Stavros-Elefsina highway.
--Social dialogue between the government, unions and employers on planned changes to the job market is no replacement for collective bargaining agreements, Labour Minister Miltiades Papaioannou says.
